August 24, 2026

Trump moves closer to declaring a national emergency over elections

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration has been rapidly declassifying election-related documents and increasing public claims about non-citizen voting, steps described as laying the groundwork for a national emergency declaration. In the past 48 hours, the USPS published a rule that would prevent states from receiving mail-in ballots if they do not provide certain information to the Postal Service. The rule has been blocked by multiple judges and is on hold, but was published anyway in case the injunctions are overturned. Experts have raised alarms as election day approaches.

US prepares what officials call an economic D-Day against Iran

tags: politics, markets
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

President Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the United States will launch an offensive economic campaign against Iran, described as an "economic D-Day." Iran responded by warning that any party aiding the United States would face severe consequences. The move comes amid an ongoing war that has been running for months.

Trump administration proposes $103,000 fee per H-1B visa

tags: immigration, politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

A rule introduced by the Department of Homeland Security and filed in the Federal Register would charge employers roughly $103,000 for each H-1B visa, up from fees in the low thousands of dollars. The rule enters the standard rulemaking process, which may take several months. Proceeds from the fee would fund the immigration enforcement system, including ICE. Employers are expected to sharply curtail hiring of foreign-born workers, particularly in the tech sector, if it takes effect.

Trump sets 50% tariffs on Canadian cars and steel as Ontario weighs cutting off electricity and minerals

tags: markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Trump announced that on January 1, 2027, tariffs on all cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel from Canada will rise to 50%, saying Canada's tariffs on American farm products have created a $60 billion deficit and that goods built in the US would face zero tariffs. Ontario Premier Doug Ford said Canada should consider cutting off critical mineral and electricity exports to the United States, saying Ontario would not supply a grain of sand. Several Midwestern states rely on Canadian electricity imports. No formal Canadian retaliation has been decided, and car prices are expected to rise if the tariffs take effect.

Navy sailor's father detained by ICE during nine-month deployment

tags: immigration, military
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Joshua Avilis, a US Navy service member aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, said he learned during his return from a nine-month Middle East deployment that his father had been taken into immigration custody. His father held a work permit, a Social Security card and a driver's license. The carrier is still weeks from returning to port. DHS carried out the detention before the sailor's return.

Israeli strikes kill four-year-old in Gaza as further attacks warned

tags: conflict, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

Israeli strikes on Gaza killed two people, including a four-year-old boy, and Israel warned that further attacks would follow. Footage of the day's strikes circulated on independent channels, which said mainstream outlets had not covered the operation. Separately, Israel's defence minister said that any further flags or kites flown into Israeli territory would be treated officially as an act of war, after the military shot down several kites.

Arbitrator orders Washington Post to rehire Karen Attiah with back pay

tags: media, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A private arbitrator ruled that the Washington Post must immediately reinstate former columnist Karen Attiah and compensate her with back pay. Attiah was fired in September over social media posts she made following the death of Charlie Kirk. Numerous people across the country were dismissed from jobs over similar posts.

White House staff departures accelerate ahead of November midterms

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Politico reported that more than five White House staffers have already left, with more expected, as officials see the writing on the wall less than 75 days before the November midterm elections. Departures include Caroline Leavitt and James Baird. Staffers reportedly expect Democrats to win control and to face investigations and subpoenas, and are seeking positions at lobbying firms.

US military resumes strikes on suspected cartel boats in the Pacific

tags: military, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

The US military struck a suspected cartel vessel in the eastern Pacific on Sunday, killing two people. The strike marks a resumption of the boat-strike campaign conducted under SOUTHCOM.

Over 30,000 still without power in Northwest Indiana after 12 days

tags: climate, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

More than 30,000 residents in Gary and Northwest Indiana remain without electricity 12 days after an outage began, with restoration not expected until Tuesday, roughly two weeks after it started. Thousands of residents are relying on local shelters for food and supplies, and schools remain closed.

Jeffries reported meeting with Kushner ahead of expected House flip

tags: politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has been meeting privately with Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, despite publicly criticising the administration. The meetings come as the House is widely expected to flip to Democratic control in November, which would likely make Jeffries Speaker. The account characterised the contacts as evidence of bipartisan continuity on foreign policy, and said Jeffries has stated he does not support expanded affordable health care.

White House promotes MAGA-branded Freedom 250 Grand Prix using Cars characters

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The official White House account posted promotional material for the Indianapolis Grand Prix, rebranded the MAGA Freedom 250 Grand Prix, using vehicles from Disney's Cars franchise. The event was originally planned as a nonpartisan celebration of the country's 250th anniversary. Questions were raised about the use of Disney intellectual property in a partisan government promotion.
